what_it_is.prose: Lockheed Martin is the largest US defence prime and a long-standing India partner across transport aircraft, naval helicopters, and missiles. Indian inventory includes: 5 (originally 6, one crashed) C-130J-30 Super Hercules tactical airlifters with IAF No. 77 Squadron 'Veiled Vipers' (with $328M fleet support contract signed Aug 2021); 24 MH-60R Seahawks for the Indian Navy with $905M initial contract (May 2020) and ₹7,995 crore follow-on deal (Dec 2025) — deliveries ongoing; and Javelin anti-tank missiles (Lockheed-Raytheon JV) under emergency procurement — 60 launchers + 100 missiles for ₹292 crore ($93M) signed August 2026. Lockheed offers F-21 (F-16V derivative) for India's MRFA 114-fighter tender; Lockheed-Tata Advanced Systems signed agreement Sep 2024 to expand C-130J opportunities in India including potential final assembly line.

faq.question: How many C-130J Super Hercules does the Indian Air Force operate?
faq.answer: The Indian Air Force originally ordered 6 C-130J-30 Super Hercules (contract signed 2008, deliveries 2010-2014) for No. 77 Squadron 'Veiled Vipers' at Hindon AFS. One aircraft crashed near Gwalior in March 2014, leaving 5 operational. In August 2021 Lockheed Martin was awarded a 5-year, $328M contract to support the fleet.

faq.question: What is the value of the Indian Navy's MH-60R Seahawk deal?
faq.answer: The Indian Navy contracted 24 MH-60R Seahawks (Sikorsky/Lockheed Martin) for $904-905 million in May 2020 via the US FMS route. A follow-on ₹7,995 crore (~$950M) deal was signed in November/December 2025 for additional support and equipment. Deliveries have been ongoing since 2024.

faq.question: Has India ordered Javelin anti-tank missiles?
faq.answer: Yes. Under emergency procurement, the Indian Army signed a ₹292 crore (~$93 million) deal in August 2026 for 60 Javelin launchers and 100 missiles from the Lockheed-Raytheon Javelin JV. A co-production MOU with Bharat Dynamics Limited was signed earlier (Feb 2020).
